observed: Harvested dedicated-carry seams from 3,842 af.exe routed netlists (2,202 containing carry; 1,005,996 carry links; 19,790 inter-tile crossings). Dedicated carry is NOT present in route.tx -- carry nets decode to an empty path -- so it was harvested from *_routed.v .Cin()/.Cout() connectivity plus defparam coord_x/y/z. Result: 113 distinct inter-tile seams, which is ALL 113 that geometrically exist (12 columns x 3 + 7 columns x 11; X13 has no LogicTiles). Every one of the 19 LogicTile columns is covered, not just X20. The least-witnessed seam still appears in 9 independent designs; the most-used is X17Y6->X17Y5 with 356, while X20Y12->X20Y11 ranks 85th of 113. Two invariants hold with ZERO exceptions across all 19,790 crossings: direction is always (x,y)->(x,y-1) (same column, one tile down) and endpoints are always SLICE15->SLICE0.
scope: Vendor-corpus OBSERVATION of seam geometry, promoted as agamemnon/chipdb/carry_seam_corpus.csv (reference data; not consumed by emission). Observing a seam in a vendor placement is NOT a conduction claim and NOT a silicon qualification -- the qualified carry surface is unchanged. What this does establish is that the restriction of AGaMEMnon's carry to three hard-coded footprints in column X20 reflects our own placer/arch, not a property of the part, and that the vendor exercises the same seam shape in every column.

next_experiment: Rebuild the already-qualified 33-site carry shape in column X15 (X15Y12->X15Y11->X15Y10), a pure column swap of a passing experiment with a matched vendor build available for byte-diffing, and separately re-run X15Y4->X15Y3 with a FULL 16-stage source tile as the strict control for the original failure.
observed: Two of the three inter-tile carry seam pips shipped in features/carry.py contradict the corpus invariant: (20,11)->(20,12) runs UPWARD and (20,12)->(20,10) SKIPS a tile, and neither shape occurs in any of the 3,842 routed vendor netlists, against 19,790 crossings that are uniformly (x,y)->(x,y-1). Separately, the vendor never crosses a seam out of a partially filled tile: all 19,790 crossings have exactly 15 upstream stages in the source tile (3 have 31), and no chain head anywhere sits at z15. The AGaMEMnon X15Y{4..9} sweep recorded as fail_isolated in carry_evidence.jsonl placed a 2-stage chain with its head AT SLICE15 -- a geometry with zero vendor precedent -- whereas the passing X20Y12->X20Y11 trial used a full 16-slice source tile, matching the invariant.
scope: Retained flag, not a retraction. The 33-stage order that uses the two unsupported pips is recorded as a silicon pass, so either the hardware is richer than the vendor placer reveals or that trial's observable (increment 0x01010101 with only lanes 0 and 1 checked) was not discriminating; this is not resolved here and no existing claim is withdrawn. It does mean the earlier per-seam 'dead' reading at X15 is better explained by an illegal head-at-SLICE15 geometry than by seam deadness -- the same shape of error as the conduction reframe.

consequence: The recorded X20 33-stage silicon pass needs re-examination on the same grounds already flagged for its two invariant-violating pips: if an inter-tile crossing needs configuration that is never emitted, a pass at X20 cannot have come from a configured dedicated seam, and that trial's observable checked only two lanes of an 0x01010101 increment.
next_experiment: Determine whether the inter-tile crossing is dedicated hardware or a routed mesh net, by decoding a vendor bitstream for a KNOWN inter-tile carry design and checking whether RMUX selectors are set along a Cout->Cin path. That settles whether AGaMEMnon must emit routing for inter-tile carry, and it is a decode question with no board time.
observed: AGaMEMnon's emitter SKIPS every carry hop: features/routing.py drops any edge whose source or destination family starts with CARRY before selector emission. So a carry pip contributes zero configuration bits to the bitstream -- including the three inter-tile seam pips shipped in features/carry.py. Confirmed empirically in the workbench: a chain crossing an inter-tile seam and the same chain confined to one tile differ by 81 config bytes, all of which are the extra slices' own per-slice config; nothing in the image configures the crossing. On silicon both froze (ahb_read_run distinct=1), as did a robust-mask variant whose control and seam builds returned byte-identical readings.
scope: CORRECTION to an earlier record in this ledger. That record stated the seam 'costs no configuration bits' and that widening carry 'needs no new chipdb'. The evidence behind it was only that seam-crossing slices carry the same PER-SLICE pattern as any other stage; that says nothing about whether the inter-tile CONNECTION requires configuration. The workbench RE notes and arch.py's own comment both state that inter-tile carry is a ROUTED MESH net (top slice Cout -> RMUX mesh -> next tile's bottom slice Cin), which would require routing configuration that is currently never emitted. The two readings contradict and are NOT resolved here. Withdrawn: 'no new chipdb / pure placer change'. Retained: the 113 observed seam geometries and the two direction/endpoint invariants, which are netlist-placement observations and unaffected.

consequence: The downward inter-tile carry seam CONDUCTS in column X15. The 2026-07-14 negative was an emission artifact, not silicon: cnt[1] leaves the fabric over X14Y12_RMUX43 -> X13Y12_BBMUXE03, and the shipped BBMUXE_PAIR carried (0,6) for source RMUX43 -- RMUX63's codeword -- instead of the vendor-harvested (1,6) in chipdb/bbmuxe_fanin.csv. The boundary mux therefore selected a track cnt[1] never drove, so the lane could not vary no matter what the carry chain did. Exactly two config bytes differ between the failing and passing images (plus the trailing CRC-32/BZIP2), and they are the BBMUXE03 selector: [0,6] -> [1,6]. The recorded resolution 'do not expose generalized downward seam pips in the release architecture' rests on a poisoned observation and is withdrawn as unproven; the architecture gate is NOT changed by this record, because one instance is not a sweep.
next_experiment: Re-run the y=4..9 X15 sweep end to end with the corrected emitter, and re-read the two --mcu tap images already built for the (14,5) seam, which currently show only one varying lane and are therefore still inconclusive.
observed: The retained X15 downward-seam artifact was re-packed with a two-byte emitter correction and re-read: STAT=0x000f0002, 500 samples, distinct=4 over the full 32-bit hrdata word (0xfffffffc/d/e/f at 126/124/125/125), varying lanes [0,1]. The dedicated crossing X15Y2_CARRYOUT15 -> X15Y1_CARRYIN00 is present in qualification/counter2_carry_seam_routed.json, the routed netlist is UNCHANGED, and the counter is uniform across all four states. The original trial recorded verdict fail_isolated with 'the upstream bit0 varied but downstream bit1 never varied'.
scope: One seam instance (X15Y2 SLICE15 -> X15Y1 SLICE0), one readout, re-packed from a retained routed artifact. It does NOT qualify generalized downward seams, other columns, or other rows, and it adds no architecture pip. It establishes that the sweep that produced the negative must be re-run before any downward-seam claim -- in either direction -- is trusted.
